keyVerseText: Behold, to morrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as hath not been in Egypt since the foundation thereof even until now.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb יָסַד (yâçad) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the idea of setting something firmly in place. Its core sense involves establishing or founding with stability and permanence, much like laying a foundation that supports what is to come. This literal sense of fixing or founding undergirds its broader figurative uses, emphasizing the act of making something sure, settled, or ordained rather than merely placing or appointing in a casual way.
usageInScripture: Throughout the 42 occurrences of יָסַד in Scripture, the word consistently appears in contexts related to founding, establishing, or laying a foundation, as reflected in its top translations such as 'to lay the foundation,' 'hath founded,' and 'he laid the foundation.' This consistency highlights its primary role in describing the act of setting something in a firm and enduring way, whether it be physical foundations or metaphorical establishments like ordinances or divine decrees. The range of meanings also includes sitting or consulting together, showing a nuanced use that involves both physical and communal or spiritual establishment.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, יָסַד reveals the divine attribute of God as the ultimate founder and establisher of all things, emphasizing His sovereign authority to ordain and fix the order of creation and covenant. Recognizing God as the one who 'lays the foundation' invites believers to trust in the stability and permanence of His purposes and promises. This verb also speaks to the believer’s call to be firmly established in faith, grounded in the sure foundation of Christ. Understanding יָסַד enriches our appreciation of God’s providential work in both the physical and spiritual realms, reminding us that all true establishment flows from His sovereign will.
keyVerseReflection: In Exodus 9:18, the phrase 'since the foundation thereof even until now' uses יָסַד to anchor the severity of the coming hailstorm in the historical and foundational reality of Egypt itself. This word conveys that the judgment about to come is unprecedented since the very establishment of the land, underscoring God's sovereign control over creation's order and history. It powerfully illustrates that God’s acts of judgment and mercy are grounded in His authority as the one who founded and sustains all things.
